from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title_text = "The Perspective Problem"
        lecture_lines = [
            "One point can have different coordinates in different grids.",
            "We describe its position using standard floor tiles.",
            "The robot uses its own tilted, custom grid."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        COLOR_STD = WHITE
        COLOR_SLANTED = "#5271FF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid 'latex' executable dependency
        
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4], 
            y_range=[-4, 4], 
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": COLOR_STD, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": COLOR_STD, "stroke_width": 1}
        )
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        pos_z4 = std_grid.c2p(2, 1)
        z4_dot = Dot(pos_z4, color=COLOR_STD)
        z4_label = Text("Z-4", font_size=24, color=COLOR_STD)
        z4_label.next_to(z4_dot, UL, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(std_grid),
            FadeIn(z4_dot),
            Write(z4_label),
            self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_STD),

        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        
        slanted_grid = NumberPlane(

        slanted_grid.apply_matrix([[2, -1], [1, 1]])
        self.place_in_area(slanted_grid, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        self.play(
            Create(slanted_grid),
            self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_STD),
            run_time=2

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        
        # Standard projections
        h_line = std_grid.get_horizontal_line(pos_z4, color=COLOR_STD, stroke_width=1)
        v_line = std_grid.get_vertical_line(pos_z4, color=COLOR_STD, stroke_width=1)
        std_coords = Text("(2, 1) std", color=COLOR_STD, font_size=24)
        std_coords.next_to(z4_dot, DR, buff=0.1)
        
        # Slanted highlight (vector along first basis direction)
        slanted_vec = Arrow(
            std_grid.get_origin(), 
            pos_z4, 
            buff=0, 
            color=COLOR_SLANTED, 
            stroke_width=4
        )
        slanted_coords = Text("(1, 0) blue", color=COLOR_SLANTED, font_size=24)
        slanted_coords.next_to(z4_dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            Create(h_line),
            Create(v_line),
            Write(std_coords),
            GrowArrow(slanted_vec),
            Write(slanted_coords),
            self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_STD),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # 1. Title and lecture lines from shared state
        title_text = "Prerequisite: What is a Basis?"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Standard basis vectors i-hat and j-hat form squares.",
            "Any two non-parallel vectors can form a new grid.",
            "Let's define a new basis with two slanted vectors."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # Colors
        I_COLOR = "#00FF00" # Green
        J_COLOR = "#FF0000" # Red
        B1_COLOR = "#00FFFF" # Cyan
        B2_COLOR = "#FFFF00" # Yellow
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Standard basis vectors i-hat and j-hat form squares.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(I_COLOR)
        
        # Visual: Standard basis (1,0) and (0,1)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            y_range=[-3, 3, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.4}
        )
        
        # Basis vectors and labels - Replaced MathTex with Text to avoid LaTeX dependency error
        i_vec = Arrow(start=plane.c2p(0,0), end=plane.c2p(1,0), buff=0, color=I_COLOR)
        j_vec = Arrow(start=plane.c2p(0,0), end=plane.c2p(0,1), buff=0, color=J_COLOR)
        i_label = Text("i", slant=ITALIC, color=I_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(i_vec, DOWN, buff=0.1)
        j_label = Text("j", slant=ITALIC, color=J_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(j_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        # Group and position in the right visual area
        viz_group = VGroup(plane, i_vec, j_vec, i_label, j_label)
        self.place_in_area(viz_group, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(plane))
        self.play(GrowArrow(i_vec), Write(i_label))
        self.play(GrowArrow(j_vec), Write(j_label))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Any two non-parallel vectors can form a new grid.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(B1_COLOR)
        
        # Morph i, j into b1=(2,1) and b2=(-1,1)
        b1_target_pos = plane.c2p(2, 1)
        b2_target_pos = plane.c2p(-1, 1)
        
        b1_vec = Arrow(start=plane.c2p(0,0), end=b1_target_pos, buff=0, color=B1_COLOR)
        b2_vec = Arrow(start=plane.c2p(0,0), end=b2_target_pos, buff=0, color=B2_COLOR)
        
        # Labels for new basis - Replaced MathTex with Text
        b1_label = Text("b1", slant=ITALIC, color=B1_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(b1_vec, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        b2_label = Text("b2", slant=ITALIC, color=B2_COLOR, font_size=24).next_to(b2_vec, LEFT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(i_vec, b1_vec),
            ReplacementTransform(i_label, b1_label),
            ReplacementTransform(j_vec, b2_vec),
            ReplacementTransform(j_label, b2_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Let's define a new basis with two slanted vectors.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(B2_COLOR)
        
        # Transform the plane to skewed
        matrix = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        
        skewed_plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            background_line_style={"stroke_opacity": 0.6}
        ).apply_matrix(matrix)
        
        # Keep same center as original plane
        skewed_plane.move_to(plane.get_center())
        
        # Morph the standard grid into the skewed coordinate system
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(plane, skewed_plane))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(Scene):
    def construct(self):
        # Helper function to create a matrix using Text since LaTeX is unavailable
        def create_text_matrix(values, color=WHITE, font_size=24):
            # Create elements as Text mobjects
            matrix_elements = VGroup(*[
                VGroup(*[Text(str(cell), font_size=font_size) for cell in row]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.5)
                for row in values
            ]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3)
            
            # Create brackets using Text and scaling them
            bracket_l = Text("[", font_size=font_size * 2).scale(1.2)
            bracket_r = Text("]", font_size=font_size * 2).scale(1.2)
            
            bracket_l.stretch_to_fit_height(matrix_elements.height + 0.2)
            bracket_r.sketch_to_fit_height = None # Cleanup check
            bracket_r.stretch_to_fit_height(matrix_elements.height + 0.2)
            
            bracket_l.next_to(matrix_elements, LEFT, buff=0.1)
            bracket_r.next_to(matrix_elements, RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            
            res = VGroup(bracket_l, matrix_elements, bracket_r).set_color(color)
            res.elements = matrix_elements # Reference for easier manipulation
            return res

        # 1. Title and Introduction
        title = Text("The Change of Basis Matrix (The Translator)", font_size=36)
        title.to_edge(UP, buff=0.5)
        
        description = Text(
            "Converts coordinates between different coordinate systems.",
            font_size=24
        ).next_to(title, DOWN, buff=0.5)

        # 2. Matrix Representation
        matrix_label = Text("Change of Basis Matrix P:", font_size=24)
        matrix_vals = [["p11", "p12"], ["p21", "p22"]]
        p_matrix = create_text_matrix(matrix_vals, color=BLUE)
        
        content_group = VGroup(matrix_label, p_matrix).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.5).center()

        # 3. Animations
        self.play(Write(title))
        self.play(FadeIn(description))
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(Write(matrix_label))
        self.play(Create(p_matrix))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Data from shared state
        title_text = "The Coordinate Transformation Formula"
        lecture_lines = [
            "We use a formula to transform between perspectives.",
            "Multiply matrix P by the robot's coordinates.",
            "This calculation maps the point back to standard space.",
            "The result tells us the standard XY coordinates.",
            "We have successfully translated the robot's location."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Use Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependencies
        formula = Text("[x]_std = P [x]_new", color=WHITE, font_size=32)
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "B5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Base standard grid for reference
        std_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-4, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE_E, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GREY_B, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(std_grid, "D2", "F5", scale_factor=0.5)
        
        # Create the skewed grid from standard using Matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]
        skewed_grid = std_grid.copy().apply_matrix([[2, -1], [1, 1]])
        skewed_grid.set_color(BLUE_C)
        
        # Vector x_new = (1, 1) in the skewed basis
        dot_pos = skewed_grid.c2p(1, 1)
        dot = Dot(dot_pos, color=YELLOW)
        dot_label = Text("[x]_new = [1, 1]", color=YELLOW, font_size=18)
        dot_label.next_to(dot, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(skewed_grid))
        self.play(FadeIn(dot), Write(dot_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        calc = Text(
            "[[2, -1], [1, 1]] * [1, 1] = [1, 2]",
            color=WHITE, font_size=24
        )
        self.place_in_area(calc, "C2", "C5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Write(calc))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        new_dot_label = Text("[x]_std = [1, 2]", color=YELLOW, font_size=18)
        new_dot_label.move_to(dot_label)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(
            ReplacementTransform(skewed_grid, std_grid),
            ReplacementTransform(dot_label, new_dot_label)
        )
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Point to the final position on the grid
        arrow = Arrow(
            start=self.grid["F6"], 
            end=dot.get_center(), 
            color=RED, 
            buff=0.1
        )
        
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Create(arrow))
        self.play(Indicate(dot))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_str = "Reversing the Process (The Inverse)"
        lecture_lines = [
            "What if we want to translate into the robot's world?",
            "We must reverse the process using the inverse matrix.",
            "Multiply standard coordinates by the inverse of P.",
            "This finds the coordinates in the robot's tilted grid.",
            "Now we can communicate directions the robot understands."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_str, lecture_lines)

        # --- Preparations ---
        # Define the Standard Grid (Standard Basis)
        standard_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE_D, "stroke_width": 1, "stroke_opacity": 0.5},
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "stroke_width": 2}
        )
        self.place_in_area(standard_grid, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Inverse Formula: [x]_new = P⁻¹ [x]_std
        formula = Text(
            "[x]_new = P⁻¹ [x]_std", 
            font_size=32,
            color=WHITE
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "B2", "B6", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        # Target Point: (3, 3) in standard basis
        point_pos = standard_grid.c2p(3, 3)
        point_std = Dot(point_pos, color=ORANGE)
        
        # Labels for the point in both bases
        point_label_std = Text("(3, 3)std", color=ORANGE, font_size=20)
        point_label_std.next_to(point_std, UR, buff=0.1)
        
        point_label_new = Text("(1, 1)new", color=GREEN, font_size=20)
        point_label_new.next_to(point_std, DR, buff=0.1)

        # New Basis Vectors (Columns of P = [[2, 1], [1, 2]])
        v1 = Arrow(start=standard_grid.c2p(0,0), end=standard_grid.c2p(2,1), buff=0, color=GREEN, stroke_width=4)
        v2 = Arrow(start=standard_grid.c2p(0,0), end=standard_grid.c2p(1,2), buff=0, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        
        # Skewed grid representing the robot's coordinate system
        skewed_grid = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            y_range=[-1, 4, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GREEN_E, "stroke_width": 2, "stroke_opacity": 0.3},
            axis_config={"stroke_width": 0}
        )
        skewed_grid.apply_matrix([[2, 1], [1, 2]])
        self.place_in_area(skewed_grid, "C2", "F6", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Add objects to the scene
        self.add(standard_grid, skewed_grid, formula, v1, v2, point_std, point_label_std, point_label_new)
        self.wait(2)

        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Fetching data for the summary section
        lecture_lines = [
            "Change of basis is simply a shift in perspective.",
            "The vector stays fixed while the grid transforms.",
            "Think of it like converting between different currencies."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Visual Recap", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(BLUE)
        
        # Standard basis grid
        grid_std = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": BLUE_E, "stroke_opacity": 0.4},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": BLUE_E}
        )
        self.place_in_area(grid_std, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Vector fixed in the scene space
        vector = Arrow(
            start=grid_std.c2p(0, 0),
            end=grid_std.c2p(1, 1),
            buff=0,
            color=RED,
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        self.play(Create(grid_std), GrowArrow(vector))
        self.wait(1)
        
        # Skewed basis grid (Basis vectors: [1, 0.5] and [0.5, 1])
        matrix = [[1, 0.5], [0.5, 1]]
        grid_skewed = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            y_range=[-2, 2, 1],
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": GOLD_E, "stroke_opacity": 0.6},
            axis_config={"stroke_color": GOLD_E}
        ).apply_matrix(matrix)
        self.place_in_area(grid_skewed, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Transform the grid background
        self.play(Transform(grid_std, grid_skewed), run_time=2)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Transition matrices labels - Using Text instead of MathTex to avoid LaTeX dependency
        p_label = Text("P", color=GREEN, slant=ITALIC)
        p_inv_label = Text("P⁻¹", color=PURPLE, slant=ITALIC)
        
        # Place labels near grid boundaries
        self.place_at_grid(p_label, 'B2', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.place_at_grid(p_inv_label, 'E5', scale_factor=1.2)
        
        # Curved arrows representing the bridge between bases
        p_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid['B2'] + UP*0.4, 
            self.grid['B5'] + UP*0.4, 
            angle=-PI/4, 
            color=GREEN
        )
        p_inv_arrow = CurvedArrow(
            self.grid['E5'] + DOWN*0.4, 
            self.grid['E2'] + DOWN*0.4, 
            angle=-PI/4, 
            color=PURPLE
        )

        self.play(
            FadeIn(p_label), 
            Create(p_arrow),
            FadeIn(p_inv_label),
            Create(p_inv_arrow)
        )
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GOLD)
        
        # Final summary text
        summary_text = Text("Change of Perspective", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_in_area(summary_text, 'F2', 'F5', scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(summary_text))
        self.wait(3)

outline.topic: Change of Basis: Translating Between Mathematical Worlds
outline.target_audience: University students or advanced high school students studying Linear Algebra

sections.title: The Perspective Problem
sections.content: Introduce the concept that the same physical point can be described by different sets of coordinates depending on the 'grid' (basis) we use. Define the goal: finding the mathematical 'translator' between these grids.
sections.example: Imagine a robot named 'Z-4' standing in a room. You describe its position using the floor tiles (Standard Basis), but the robot describes positions based on its own slanted orientation (Custom Basis). The physical robot hasn't moved, but the numbers in our reports are different.

sections.title: Prerequisite: What is a Basis?
sections.content: Briefly refresh the concept of basis vectors. Visualize the standard basis (i-hat, j-hat) as a perfect square grid. Explain that any two non-parallel vectors can form a new coordinate system (a new grid).
sections.example: Visual: An animation showing the standard i=(1,0), j=(0,1) grid morphing/tilting into a new grid defined by vectors b1=(2,1) and b2=(-1,1).

sections.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Translator)
sections.content: Explain how to build the 'Transition Matrix' (P). Key Concept: The columns of this matrix are simply the new basis vectors expressed in the language of the old (standard) basis.
sections.example: If our new basis vectors are B1 = [2, 1] and B2 = [-1, 1], we line them up to create Matrix P = [[2, -1], [1, 1]]. This matrix 'translates' coordinates from the Robot's language back to our Standard language.

sections.title: The Coordinate Transformation Formula
sections.content: Introduce the formula: [x]_{standard} = P * [x]_{new}. Visualize this as taking a coordinate in the skewed grid and 'scaling/rotating' it back to the square grid.
sections.example: If the Robot says it is at position (1, 1) in its own grid, we multiply Matrix P by [1, 1]. Calculation: [2-1, 1+1] = (1, 2). Graphically show the point landing on (1, 2) on the standard XY plane.

sections.title: Reversing the Process (The Inverse)
sections.content: How do we go from Standard Basis to the New Basis? Introduce the inverse matrix (P⁻¹). Explain that if P takes us 'Home', P⁻¹ takes us 'Into the New World'.
sections.example: To tell the robot to move to our point (3, 3), we don't give it (3, 3). We multiply (3, 3) by the inverse of P to find the coordinates in the robot's specific tilted grid.

sections.title: Summary & Visual Recap
sections.content: Summarize that 'Change of Basis' is just a change of perspective. The Transition Matrix is the bridge between these perspectives. Show a final animation of a vector staying still while the background grid swaps between standard and custom.
sections.example: Analogy: It's like converting currency. The 'Value' (the vector) stays the same, but the 'Units' (the basis) change depending on which country (coordinate system) you are in.

storyboard.title: The Change of Basis Matrix (The Translator)
lecture_lines: Matrix P acts as a translator between these grids.
We build P using the new basis vectors.
Each new vector becomes a column in Matrix P.
These columns are written in the standard basis language.
This matrix connects the robot's world to ours.
animations: Display vectors b1=(2,1) in cyan (#00FFFF) and b2=(-1,1) in yellow (#FFFF00) as independent vectors.

Box the entire matrix P and label it 'Transition Matrix' in white (#FFFFFF).

storyboard.title: The Coordinate Transformation Formula
lecture_lines: We use a formula to transform between perspectives.
Multiply matrix P by the robot's coordinates.
This calculation maps the point back to standard space.
The result tells us the standard XY coordinates.
We have successfully translated the robot's location.
animations: Write the formula [x]_std = P * [x]_new at the top in white (#FFFFFF).
Show a vector x_new=(1,1) as a dot relative to the skewed grid lines.

Animate the skewed grid morphing back into the standard square grid.
Point to the final position (1,2) on the standard square grid.

storyboard.title: Reversing the Process (The Inverse)
lecture_lines: To go the other way, use the inverse matrix.
Multiply standard coordinates by this inverse matrix.
This finds the coordinates in the robot's world.
animations: Display the inverse formula [x]_new = P⁻¹ * [x]_std in white (#FFFFFF).
Plot a point at (3,3) in the standard grid in orange (#FFA500).
Show the point's coordinates in the skewed grid after applying the inverse matrix P⁻¹.
